hero.eyebrow: A new way to observe yourself
hero.subtitle: Explore different dimensions of your mind and behaviour.

statement.copy: Each assessment reveals a new dimension of how you think, feel, decide and interact. NURA connects those discoveries without reducing who you are to a score.

featured.copy: Explore how your attention works day to day. Look at patterns related to attention, organisation, impulsivity and routine through a quick, structured experience.
featured.note: A screening and self-knowledge tool. The result does not constitute a medical diagnosis.

attention.title: ADHD: self-report for adults
attention.description: Attention, organisation and impulsivity in everyday life.

landing.metaTitle: ADHD self-report for adults — free screening | NURA
landing.metaDescription: Free adult ADHD self-report using the ASRS-v1.1 scale from the World Health Organization. 18 items, 3 to 5 minutes, no card required. A screening instrument — not a diagnosis.
landing.intro: A structured experience for observing how your attention behaves day to day: where it holds, where it slips, and which patterns repeat. The initial result is free and immediate.
landing.forWhom: For adults who recognise persistent difficulty with focus, organisation or impulse regulation and want to understand those patterns better — out of curiosity, or as a step before a professional assessment.
landing.methodology: This self-report uses the ASRS-v1.1 (Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale), developed by the World Health Organization in partnership with Harvard Medical School. It has 18 items: the first six form Part A, the screening block that flags patterns consistent with ADHD; the remaining twelve detail inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity.
landing.disclaimer: This is a screening and self-knowledge tool. The result is informative, does not constitute a medical diagnosis and does not replace assessment by a qualified professional.

landing.lead: How does your attention work day to day?
landing.limits: This is a screening instrument, not a diagnostic one. Anxiety, depression, stress and sleep deprivation produce similar symptoms and can cause false positives. Confirmation requires a clinical assessment with a psychiatrist or psychologist. Intended for people aged 18 and over.

profile.copy: Your assessments progressively build your NURA Profile: a living map of explored dimensions, nodes and connections. Never a universal score — only how much of yourself you have explored here.
profile.legend: The percentages represent how much of the NURA ecosystem you have explored. They do not mean intelligence, health or diagnosis.

trust.title: Assessments built responsibly.
trust.copy: Personal discovery only makes sense with context, clear limits and respect for the person on the other side.

information.title: Information, not a verdict
information.copy: Results are informative. Screening instruments do not replace professional diagnosis.

privacy.title: Your data, your choice
privacy.copy: Transparency about purpose, consent, deletion and care in how your data is handled.

methodology.title: Transparent methodology
methodology.copy: An experience built to encourage self-knowledge, without promising impossible precision.

diagnosis.question: Does NURA provide a diagnosis?
diagnosis.answer: No. NURA's experiences are informative and meant for self-knowledge. Some instruments can work as screening, but no result replaces a professional assessment or diagnosis.

price.question: Do I have to pay to start?
price.answer: No. You can start for free and receive an initial result. If you want to go further, the in-depth report costs R$ 19.90 as a one-time payment, with no automatic subscription.

data.question: How is my data handled?
data.answer: Privacy is part of the experience. We collect only what is needed to deliver your result, with transparency about the purpose and responsibility in how data is processed.

duration.question: How long does an assessment take?
duration.answer: It depends on the experience. The ADHD assessment for adults, for example, takes roughly 3 to 5 minutes.

finalCta.eyebrow: The next discovery can start now
finalCta.title: There is still a lot for you to discover.
finalCta.copy: Start with one question. The rest of your profile builds along the way.

footer.copy: A thoughtful experience for anyone who wants to observe themselves with more curiosity.
footer.tagline: Made to discover, not to label.

runner.introTitle: How you answer matters more than the score.
runner.introLead: {count} questions about how your attention behaves over the last six months. It takes 3 to 5 minutes.
runner.noteHonest: Answer for your actual day to day, not for how you would like to be.
runner.noteNoRightAnswer: There is no right or wrong answer — each option describes a frequency.
runner.noteResume: If you leave, your answers stay saved on this device for 7 days.
runner.disclaimer: A screening and self-knowledge instrument. The result is informative, is not a diagnosis and does not replace assessment by a qualified professional.
runner.resume: Pick up where I left off
runner.resumeFound: You have already answered {answered} of 18 questions.
runner.answerAll: Answer every question on this step to continue.
runner.transitionLead: The next questions do not change the screening result. They describe which patterns showed up, and that is what gives your report depth.
runner.doneLead: Your result is being prepared. The result screen arrives in the next development step.
runner.unavailableTitle: This assessment is not available in this language yet.
runner.unavailableLead: The scale used here only has an officially validated translation in Portuguese. Translating it ourselves would void the scientific validation, so we would rather not offer it.
runner.contextTitle: Tell us a little about your context.
runner.contextLead: Three quick questions to personalise how your result is presented.
runner.contextNoScore: These are NURA's questions, not the scale's. They do not change your result — you can skip them.

result_screen.title: What your answers showed.
result_screen.screenCount: {count} of 6 answers in the attention range
result_screen.notElevatedTitle: No elevated pattern showed up in this screening.
result_screen.notElevatedSummary: By the Part A criterion, your answers fell below the cutoff. That does not rule ADHD out or end the conversation: screenings have limits, and symptoms can present in ways this instrument does not capture.
result_screen.highlyConsistentTitle: Your patterns warrant a closer look.
result_screen.highlyConsistentSummary: By the Part A criterion, your answers fell in the range the instrument describes as highly consistent with ADHD. That is a signal, not a diagnosis — confirmation requires a clinical assessment with a psychiatrist or psychologist.
result_screen.domainsLead: These are the items you answered in the clinically relevant range, grouped by symptom type. They describe; they do not score.
result_screen.nextElevated: Take this result to a professional. A psychiatrist, neurologist or psychologist experienced in adult ADHD can investigate the criteria a questionnaire cannot reach: when the signs started, how many contexts they appear in, and what else might explain them.
result_screen.nextNotElevated: If the signs keep getting in the way day to day, seeing a professional still makes sense. Anxiety, depression, stress and sleep deprivation produce similar symptoms and deserve the same attention.
result_screen.premiumTitle: Want to understand this result in depth?
